name: Maximizing Privacy for Attached ADU Additions on Small Los Angeles County Lots

mainEntity.name: How can an ADU additions contractor in Los Angeles County help maximize privacy between the main home and a new attached ADU on a small lot?
mainEntity.text: How can an ADU additions contractor in Los Angeles County help maximize privacy between the main home and a new attached ADU on a small lot?

acceptedAnswer.text: Small Los Angeles County lots make privacy between an attached ADU addition and the main home especially challenging. A thoughtful ADU additions contractor works with the designer to align openings and circulation paths for privacy. Techniques include placing windows so they do not directly face each other or neighboring properties, using frosted, obscured, or clerestory windows near shared property lines, and orienting living areas away from the main home’s most active spaces. Separate, offset entries reduce the sense of shared thresholds, and short privacy fences, trellises, or landscape screens can block direct sightlines without making the yard feel closed in. Inside, creating buffer zones—such as closets, bathrooms, or storage rooms—between bedrooms in the main home and noisy areas in the ADU adds both visual and acoustic separation. Stair and hallway placement can direct foot traffic away from private outdoor areas. Overhead, covered porches or pergolas can block views into windows from upper‑level additions. Discuss your privacy concerns explicitly with your contractor and ask them to review sightlines on the plans before permits are submitted. Addressing these issues in design is more effective than trying to solve them with blinds or curtains after construction.
acceptedAnswer.description: Contractors can enhance privacy on small lots by orienting windows away from each other, using frosted or clerestory glass, creating offset entries, and adding fences or screens. Interior planning with buffered zones like closets between units also reduces visual and acoustic intrusion.
